summary: Episode 35 covers Ta'if, the day the Prophet ﷺ called the hardest of his life, after the deaths of Khadijah RA and Abu Talib. The ustaz starts with Abu Lahab, who offered protection then withdrew it, and the story of the filth placed on the Prophet's ﷺ shoulders while he prostrated, with Fatimah RA cleaning it off. The Prophet ﷺ then walked about 150 km to Ta'if with Zaid ibn Harithah, met three Ta'if leaders, was insulted and stoned until he bled. In an orchard he made a supplication that complained of his weakness to Allah and affirmed 'as long as You are not angry with me, I do not care'. Addas of Nineveh accepted Islam, the angel of the mountains offered to crush Ta'if but the Prophet ﷺ chose to hope in their descendants. The ustaz closes with lessons for today: cancel culture, cyberbullying and children's emotions, and a reminder ahead of Ramadan.
keyPoints: After Abu Talib's death (outer protection) and Khadijah's (inner calm), the Prophet ﷺ lost his 'safe places', and Abu Lahab offered protection only briefly before withdrawing it.
The Prophet ﷺ was prostrating when filth was placed on his shoulders, and the young Fatimah RA came, crying, to clean it off.
Ta'if was chosen strategically: an independent political and economic centre and a rival to Mecca. The Prophet ﷺ walked with Zaid, was rejected by three leaders and stoned until he bled.
The supplication in the orchard teaches the etiquette of complaint: 'to You I complain of my weakness', and 'as long as You are not angry with me, I do not care', without questioning destiny.
Guidance belongs to Allah: Addas of Nineveh accepted Islam with a single 'Bismillah', and the Prophet ﷺ was reminded through the story of Prophet Yunus (Al-Qalam 68:48 to 50).

When the angel of the mountains offered to destroy Ta'if, the Prophet ﷺ refused and hoped that from their descendants would come people who worship Allah. Ta'if later became Muslim and the home of Ibn Abbas's teaching.

chapters.summary: An opening clip on the supplication 'to whom have You entrusted me', and 'as long as You are not angry with me, I do not care'.

chapters.title: Introduction: the lowest point in the Prophet's ﷺ life
chapters.summary: Episode 35, the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah RA in Ramadan, and the Prophet ﷺ rarely going out except to pray before the Kaaba.

chapters.title: Abu Lahab and the brief protection
chapters.summary: Abu Lahab offered protection to win a name, but withdrew it after the Quraysh baited him about Abu Talib's fate.

chapters.title: Filth on the Prophet's ﷺ shoulders during prostration
chapters.summary: Hadith of Ibn Mas'ud RA: Abu Jahl's challenge, Uqbah placing the filth, and the Prophet ﷺ staying in prostration.

chapters.title: Fatimah RA and the prayer against seven men
chapters.summary: The young Fatimah removed the filth, crying. The Prophet ﷺ comforted her and named seven men, who were later killed at Badr.

chapters.title: Walking to Ta'if with Zaid ibn Harithah
chapters.summary: A journey of about 150 km on foot, without Abu Bakr, Umar or Hamzah, and who Zaid ibn Harithah was to the Prophet ﷺ and Khadijah RA.

chapters.title: Why Ta'if? A da'wah strategy
chapters.summary: Ta'if as an independent political and economic centre, rich in grapes and roses, and a rival of Mecca. The Prophet ﷺ stayed ten days.

chapters.title: The three Ta'if leaders and the insults
chapters.summary: Three brothers, Abd Yalil, Mas'ud and Habib, gave hurtful answers, and the Prophet's ﷺ request that they not tell the Quraysh was refused.

chapters.title: Stoned until Qarn al-Tha'alib
chapters.summary: Boys were incited to throw stones, the Prophet's ﷺ feet bled, Zaid shielded him, and the Prophet ﷺ lost consciousness until he reached an orchard.

chapters.title: The orchard supplication and the danger of sulking with God
chapters.summary: The Prophet ﷺ leaned against a tree and prayed. The ustaz mentions messages from people who feel their prayers go unanswered.

chapters.title: The content: I complain, do not be angry, the light of Your face
chapters.summary: The supplication line by line: complaining of weakness, 'Lord of the weak', fearing Allah may be angry, seeking refuge in the light of His face.

chapters.title: Addas of Nineveh
chapters.summary: Utbah and Shaybah sent Addas with grapes. Addas heard 'Bismillah', said he was a Christian from Nineveh, and accepted Islam.

chapters.title: Lessons of Surah Al-Qalam and Prophet Yunus
chapters.summary: Why a man from Prophet Yunus's town. Al-Qalam 68:48 to 50 and the supplication of Dhun-Nun.

chapters.title: The angel of the mountains and forgiveness
chapters.summary: Jibril and the angel of the mountains offered to crush two mountains, but the Prophet ﷺ hoped Allah would bring from them descendants who worship Him.

chapters.title: Ta'if later: Thaqif, Ibn Abbas and Az-Zukhruf 31
chapters.summary: Ta'if was among the last tribes to accept Islam, after bargaining, the Prophet's ﷺ treatment of the delegation, Ta'if becoming Muslim and Ibn Abbas's home, and the reason of 'two great towns'.

chapters.title: Social impact: we too may be stone-throwers
chapters.summary: Cancel culture and cyberbullying, children's emotions and empathy, the word zur ahead of Ramadan, and making things easy for new Muslims.

books.context: Source of the details of the insults at Ta'if, what the Prophet ﷺ recited when stoned, his words to Fatimah, and the text of the Ta'if supplication.
Named by the ustaz as a source that the Prophet ﷺ stayed in Ta'if ten days, and which also records the Ta'if supplication.

Source of the hadith of the filth on the Prophet's ﷺ shoulders (Ibn Mas'ud) and the hadith of the angel of the mountains (Aisha). The ustaz says the Bukhari version is brief like a 'trailer', while the details come from sirah narrations.
Cited for the point that the Prophet ﷺ certainly made the Ta'if supplication even though it has no connected chain.
books.note: Title and full author name not mentioned in the lecture.

books.context: The book the ustaz will accompany through that Ramadan, so that we understand the Prophet ﷺ was not always seeking war, and how the sirah must be used with care.
Linked to empathy: people without empathy often did not have secure attachment and were bullied from childhood.
A parenting consultant's site the ustaz suggests looking at, on the effects of filming and spreading images of embarrassed children.
A collection of the Prophet's ﷺ guidance, including the journey to Ta'if.
A complete sirah summary with sections on Ta'if and the Year of Sorrow.

people.context: Hated the Prophet ﷺ, but after Abu Talib's death offered protection to win a name, then withdrew it when the Quraysh provoked him about Abu Talib's fate.
Witnessed the filth incident and said he was unable to do anything. Narrator of the hadith of the prayer against seven men.
Abu Jahl challenged, and Uqbah, described as the most wretched, placed the filth on the Prophet ﷺ while he prostrated.
Still young when she removed the filth from behind her father, crying, and scolded them. Called 'ummu abiha'.
The Prophet's ﷺ political protector. His death left him without protection from outside threats.

people.role: Adopted son of the Prophet ﷺ
people.context: Given by Khadijah to the Prophet ﷺ, he knew Khadijah better than he knew the Prophet ﷺ. Walked with him and shielded him from the stones.
Gave the Prophet ﷺ inner calm, and gave Zaid ibn Harithah to him as a gift.
Brothers who ruled jointly. Each gave a hurtful answer and incited boys to throw stones.
Was not with the Prophet ﷺ to Ta'if, because he had been badly beaten earlier when he rescued the Prophet ﷺ from being strangled with a cloth.
Was at the family orchard in Ta'if, felt pity on seeing the Prophet ﷺ, and sent Addas with grapes. Later killed at Badr.
Heard 'Bismillah', recognised Prophet Yunus, kissed the Prophet's ﷺ hands and feet, and according to the ustaz was the first to accept Islam in Ta'if.
The Prophet ﷺ called him 'my brother'. His story in Al-Qalam calmed him, and his supplication, the supplication of Dhun-Nun, resembles the Prophet's ﷺ supplication at Ta'if.
Offered to crush two mountains on Ta'if, but the Prophet ﷺ refused.

people.role: Companion, cousin of the Prophet ﷺ
people.context: Among the most learned Companions, moved to Ta'if and taught thousands of the Successors. His mosque is still in Ta'if.

people.role: A Ta'if figure who accepted Islam
people.context: Mughirah was sent to demolish the idol Lat, and mocked those who thought it would take revenge.

lessons.title: Complain to Allah without questioning destiny
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ asked 'to whom have You entrusted me', but as if complaining, not objecting to His decree.

lessons.title: As long as Allah is not angry, other hardships don't matter
lessons.body: The peak of love for Allah: 'as long as You are not angry with me, I do not care', and His well-being is wide enough.

lessons.title: Worry about yourself, not blame Allah
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ felt there might be a fault that brought Allah's anger, whereas we often feel 'deserving' and blame Him. The ustaz mentions messages from people who say God cheats or only answers the prayers of hypocrites, and this opens a door for the devil.

lessons.title: Even those who hurt you can be moved
lessons.body: Utbah and Shaybah, who laughed at the Prophet ﷺ in Mecca, felt pity for him in Ta'if because he was 'one of our own'.

lessons.title: Safe places disappear, but reliance is only on Allah
lessons.body: Abu Talib protected from outside and Khadijah calmed from within. When both were gone, the Prophet ﷺ was trained to rely wholly on Allah, says the ustaz, as wisdom before the Isra' Mi'raj.

lessons.title: Choose da'wah targets strategically
lessons.body: Ta'if was chosen because it was an independent political and economic centre, and if it accepted, it would be a strong base rivalling Mecca.

lessons.title: Give full attention to the person in front of us
lessons.body: The ustaz admits people often feel ignored when the other answers messages or looks elsewhere, and admires how the Prophet ﷺ made everyone feel attended to.

lessons.title: Words can hurt more than stones
lessons.body: Scholars say the answers of the Ta'if leaders were more painful than the stoning, and the tongue can pierce more than a knife.

lessons.title: Guidance belongs to Allah, not dependent on closeness
lessons.body: Abu Talib, who raised the Prophet ﷺ, did not accept Islam, but Addas, who came from far away, accepted Islam with a single 'Bismillah'.

lessons.title: In hardship, pray with the supplication of Prophet Yunus
lessons.body: The supplication of Dhun-Nun and Prophet Yunus's patience are a guide. The Prophet ﷺ gave an assurance that Allah will relieve anyone in difficulty who prays with it.

lessons.title: Forgive and hope in the descendants of the enemy
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ refused to crush Ta'if and hoped that from their descendants would come people who worship Allah. The ustaz calls this a level of forgiveness no other human could reach.

lessons.title: Patience in da'wah eventually bears fruit
lessons.body: Ta'if finally became fully Muslim and a place of learning, including Ibn Abbas. The ustaz recalls the Prophet ﷺ held back the distribution of the Ta'if spoils for 40 days, waiting for them to accept Islam.

lessons.title: Material advantage can blur the truth
lessons.body: The Quraysh and Ta'if measured honour by wealth, and rejected a Prophet who was not rich. The poor of Madinah welcomed him gladly.

lessons.title: Don't be a stone-thrower in the digital age
lessons.body: We may be stone-throwers when we cancel and shame people with algorithms, and tear down dignity without evidence. The ustaz also reminds us of the emotional effect on children who are bullied and filmed, and suggests the book Being There.

lessons.title: Make it easy for new Muslims
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ accepted early offers such as two prayers a day because he knew their psychology, intending that they would reach five. The ustaz gives the example of a young new Muslim who felt overburdened.

glossary.meaning: The Year of Sorrow, the year of the loss of Abu Talib and Khadijah RA and the Ta'if incident.
'Mother of her father', the title of Fatimah RA for caring for the Prophet ﷺ in his hardship.
The greatest idol of the people of Ta'if, adorned with jewels and gold, and later demolished.
A place outside Ta'if where the Prophet ﷺ came to after being stoned, covered in blood.
'Lord of the weak', a title in the Prophet's ﷺ supplication at Ta'if.
There is no power and no strength except with Allah, a treasure of Paradise for this community.
The supplication of Prophet Yunus: there is no god but You, glory be to You, I was among the wrongdoers.
The angel of the mountains who offered to crush two mountains on Ta'if.
The tribe of the people of Ta'if. Among the last tribes to accept Islam, after bargaining.
False and vile speech that leads to wrongdoing and tears down dignity.

dalil.context: The ustaz says Abdullah ibn Mas'ud witnessed it and said he could do nothing. The ustaz also uses it to show that a system held by an elite can restrain even those in power.
dalil.translation: Abu Jahl challenged who would put the entrails of a slaughtered camel on the shoulders of the Prophet ﷺ while he prostrated. Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt did it and they laughed uproariously. The Prophet ﷺ stayed in prostration without lifting his head until Fatimah came and cleaned it off.

dalil.context: The ustaz says some scholars link Fatimah to her courage and the painful experience of accompanying her father from childhood. She was called 'ummu abiha'.
dalil.translation: The greatest women are Asiyah, Maryam, Khadijah and Fatimah.

dalil.context: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud swore he saw them thrown into the dry well after the Battle of Badr. The ustaz notes two of them reappear in the Ta'if story.
dalil.translation: O Allah, destroy Abu Jahl, Utbah, Shaybah, Al-Walid, Umayyah and Uqbah.

dalil.context: The ustaz says this supplication has no connected chain but sirah scholars affirm that the Prophet ﷺ certainly made it. It appears in Ibn Hisham, Ibn Sa'd and Prof. Quraish's book. The translation here is a summary from the ustaz's reading.
dalil.translation: O Allah, to You I complain of the weakness of my strength, my lack of means, and my lowliness before people. O Most Merciful, You are the Lord of the weak and You are my Lord. To whom do You entrust me, to a distant one who frowns at me or to an enemy to whom You have given control over my affairs? If You are not angry with me, I do not care, but Your well-being is wider for me. I seek refuge in the light of Your face, by which all darkness is illuminated and the affairs of this world and the next are set right, from Your anger descending upon me. To You belongs all contentment until You are pleased, and there is no power and no strength except with You.

dalil.context: The ustaz links it to the closing of the Prophet's ﷺ supplication at Ta'if.
dalil.translation: The words 'there is no power and no strength except with Allah' are a treasure from the treasures of Paradise granted to this community.

dalil.context: A sirah narration. Addas bowed and kissed the head, hands and feet of the Prophet ﷺ, and according to the ustaz was the first to accept Islam in Ta'if.
dalil.translation: When Addas said he was from Nineveh, the Prophet ﷺ said, that is the town of the righteous servant, Yunus ibn Matta. He is my brother, he was a prophet and so am I.

dalil.context: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to be patient with his Lord's decree and not be like 'the companion of the fish', Prophet Yunus. The ustaz mentions surah 68 and verses 48 to 50.
dalil.translation: Wait patiently [Prophet] for your Lord’s judgement: do not be like the man in the whale who called out in distress:

dalil.context: Prophet Yunus's supplication in hardship: 'There is no god but You, glory be to You, I was among the wrongdoers'. The ustaz says this resembles the Prophet's ﷺ supplication at Ta'if, and the Prophet ﷺ said whoever prays with it will be relieved by Allah. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: And remember the man with the whale,when he went off angrily, thinking We could not restrict him, but then he cried out in the deep darkness, ‘There is no God but You, glory be to You, I was wrong.’

dalil.context: The supplication of Dhun-Nun is 'La ilaha illa anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu minaz zalimin'. The ustaz links the Prophet ﷺ at Ta'if with Prophet Yunus, who left his people.
dalil.translation: Whoever in distress prays with the supplication of Prophet Yunus, Allah relieves him of any distress.

dalil.context: Had the favour of his Lord not reached him, he would have been cast onto barren land in disgrace. The ustaz stresses that Allah does not blame Yunus.
dalil.translation: if his Lord’s grace had not reached him, he would have been left, abandoned and blameworthy, on the barren shore,

dalil.context: His Lord chose him and made him among the righteous.
dalil.translation: but his Lord chose him and made him one of the Righteous.

dalil.context: The ustaz stresses that had the Prophet ﷺ merely said 'go ahead', Ta'if would not exist today.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ told Aisha about the hardest day. After he was stoned until he lost consciousness, Jibril and the angel of the mountains offered to crush two mountains on the people of Ta'if. The Prophet ﷺ replied, rather I hope that Allah will bring from their descendants those who worship Allah alone, associating nothing with Him.

dalil.context: The Quraysh and Ta'if said why was the Quran not sent down to a prominent man from one of the two great towns, Mecca or Ta'if. They measured honour by material things.
dalil.translation: and they said, ‘Why was this Quran not sent down to a distinguished man, from either of the two cities?’

dalil.context: The ustaz gives a reminder ahead of Ramadan so that fasting does not become an 'empty fast'.
dalil.translation: Whoever does not give up false speech, which leads to wrongdoing and tears down dignity, Allah has no need of his giving up food and drink.

dalil.context: The ustaz closes the lecture by inviting us to send blessings as thanks for his sacrifice.
dalil.translation: The angels deliver each of our blessings specifically to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ knows who sends blessings upon him.

sirah.era: Amul Huzn: the Year of Sorrow, before the Isra' Mi'raj
sirah.summary: After the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah RA, the Prophet ﷺ lost protection and calm. The ustaz tells of the hardest day at Ta'if and how he answered it with supplication, patience and forgiveness.

events.label: Ta'if
